newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Hundreds hurt in recent Afghan fighting - Red Cross.
newsitem.headline: Hundreds hurt in recent Afghan fighting - Red Cross.

text.p: At least 800 people have been wounded in recent fighting in Afghanistan and hospitals are full of new victims from the frontline north of the capital Kabul, the International Committee of the Red Cross said on Wednesday.

Some 300 casualties were taken to six main Kabul hospitals in just five days up to October 11, and more than 300 others were airlifted to the town of Kandahar on October 12-13 by Islamic Taleban fighters, the Geneva-based ICRC said in a statement.
Another 194 patients were taken on Monday to Kandahar's Mirwais hospital where the ICRC reinforced its surgical staff following the latest influx, the statement added.
The Taleban took Kabul on September 27, ousting former government military chief Ahmad Shah Masood who withdrew from the city as the Islamic fighters moved in.
On Wednesday, Taleban warplanes bombed the strategic town of Jabal os-Siraj held by Masood, witnesses said.
Jabal os-Siraj sits 90 km (60 miles) north of Kabul astride the main highway linking Kabul to northern Afghanistan where the ICRC said it had been bringing out victims every day.
